recipes.name: Quick look
recipes.summary: The 1,000 most common ports, with service names. Where most scans should start.
recipes.when: You want to know what is listening, now, and you do not have root.

recipes.name: Every TCP port
recipes.summary: All 65,535 ports. Slower, but the only way to find a service hiding high up.
recipes.when: The quick look found little and you suspect something on an odd port.

recipes.name: Services and operating system
recipes.summary: Version detection plus OS fingerprinting on the common ports.
recipes.when: You know what is open and now want to know what it is running.

recipes.name: Everything at once
recipes.summary: -A turns on OS detection, version detection, default scripts and traceroute together.
recipes.when: An authorised box you control, and you want the full picture in one command.
recipes.cost: Slow and very loud. Needs root.

recipes.name: Which hosts are up
recipes.summary: Host discovery only — no port scan. Maps a subnet before you scan anything in it.
recipes.when: First command against a new network.

recipes.name: Scan hosts that ignore ping
recipes.summary: Skips discovery and scans anyway. Firewalls often drop ICMP while leaving ports open.
recipes.when: nmap says "host seems down" but you know it is not.
recipes.cost: Slower, because nothing is skipped early. Needs root.

recipes.name: List targets without touching them
recipes.summary: Expands the target specification and resolves names. Sends nothing to the hosts.
recipes.when: Checking that a range means what you think before you scan it.
recipes.cost: Instant, and nothing reaches the targets.

recipes.name: Slow and quiet
recipes.summary: SYN scan at the sneaky timing template, which waits between probes to stay under rate-based detection.
recipes.when: The target has monitoring and you would rather not trip it.
recipes.cost: Minutes to hours — that is the point. Needs root.

recipes.name: Fragmented packets
recipes.summary: Splits probes into tiny IP fragments, which some older filters fail to reassemble.
recipes.when: A packet filter is dropping ordinary probes.
recipes.cost: Needs root. Modern firewalls reassemble, so expect this to be detected.

recipes.name: Hide among decoys
recipes.summary: Sends probes that appear to come from other addresses as well as yours, so the log is crowded.
recipes.when: You want your address to be one of several in the target's logs.
recipes.cost: Needs root. Your real address is still in there.

recipes.name: Come from a trusted port
recipes.summary: Sets the source port to 53. Some firewalls trust DNS traffic by rule.
recipes.when: Egress or ingress rules appear to be port-based.

recipes.name: Default scripts
recipes.summary: Runs NSE's default set against open ports — banners, titles, certificates, shares.
recipes.when: Standard follow-up once you know what is open.

recipes.name: Known vulnerability checks
recipes.summary: Runs the vuln category, which tests for specific published weaknesses.
recipes.when: You have authorisation and want known issues flagged automatically.
recipes.cost: Slow, noisy, and some scripts are intrusive. Needs root.

recipes.name: Windows and SMB shares
recipes.summary: Targets the SMB ports and runs the SMB enumeration scripts.
recipes.when: A Windows host or a file server is in scope.

recipes.name: Save the results
recipes.summary: Writes normal, XML and grepable output at once, so you can read it now and parse it later.
recipes.when: Any scan whose results you will need again — which is most of them.
recipes.cost: Needs root. Writes scan.nmap, scan.xml and scan.gnmap.

recipes.name: Common UDP ports
recipes.summary: UDP is slow to scan and easy to forget, and DNS, SNMP and TFTP all live there.
recipes.when: A TCP scan came back thin, or you are after DNS/SNMP specifically.
recipes.cost: Slow even at 100 ports — UDP has no handshake to speed things up. Needs root.
